standard_prerequisites: Context span 3993-4008: P = k[u, u^{-1}, y, x_n for n in Z] with the Z-action generated by tau(u) = u, tau(y) = u y, tau(x_n) = x_{n+1}; V(I_d) with I_d = ((1 - u^d) y, x_n - x_{n+d}) is the fix locus of tau^d; localizing at S generated by y and all 1 - u^d makes Z act freely on U = Spec(S^{-1}P); X = U/Z is the quotient algebraic space (Spaces, definition-quotient)

Context span 4010-4018: the primes p_n = (x_n, x_{n+1}, ...) in S^{-1}P satisfy tau(p_n) = p_{n+1}, so they define points xi_n of U with one common image x in X; the specializations xi_n leads to xi_{n-1} hold in U; the context concludes U -> X is an example of the promised type
core_obligations: The free Z-action on U makes the quotient map f = U -> X an etale morphism of algebraic spaces (a free action of the constant group scheme Z is an etale equivalence relation, the standard quotient fact underlying Spaces, definition-quotient, as used by the context)
The context exhibits a nontrivial chain of specializations xi_n leads to xi_{n-1} in |U| whose members all map to the single point x of X
Hence f(x) = f(x') for the distinct specialized points, proving the lemma with X = U, Y = X
proof_roadmap: Instantiate the context quotient U -> X and recall the free-action etaleness
Take the context specialization chain in the fibre over x
Read off equal images from tau(p_n) = p_{n+1}
